connectionType: blocked combinatorial information under measurement intervention and incomplete provenance
commonStructure: A latent state can be tested only through distinguishable outcomes inside exchangeable experimental blocks. The number and timing of observations change both statistical information and, potentially, the physical process; a file inventory is insufficient unless it also identifies which records belong to the declared scientific cohort.

verifiedEvidence.combinatorialCeiling: Twelve independent four-cell blocks contain at most 72 within-block pairs, so no inspection cadence can meet a 100-pair gate without increasing block size or making a stronger exchangeability assumption.
verifiedEvidence.exactDesign: Under an exact empirical-resampling calculation with lifetime spread compressed to one quarter and every integer grid phase tested, 24 usable events require a 25-cycle endpoint register; 36 usable events permit 50 cycles.
verifiedEvidence.lineage: Aurora's RO-Crate has 599 graph entities and consistently inventories 199 cell directories and 398 BDF file entities, but encodes no LFP or Figure 7 cohort relation. The paper reports 36 LFP cells while per-cell metadata explicitly identify 32.
verifiedEvidence.measurement: Published condition-based RPT work shows that capacity-loss triggers can control test burden, but it does not establish equivalence of degradation under the proposed dense endpoint register.

conditionsForTransfer: All compared cells must share a declared stress condition and an exchangeable production or assembly block.
A machine-readable manifest must bind every scientific cohort member to specimen, protocol, metadata, and result files before outcomes are inspected.
The feature register and endpoint register must remain separate so denser endpoint measurements cannot redefine the candidate coordinate.
Pair power must be calculated against narrower-than-development lifetime spreads and unfavorable grid phase, not only the observed development alignment.
A separate pilot must bound how the measurement schedule changes degradation before endpoint density is treated as passive observation.
breakConditions: Pooling pairs across unequal conditions to exceed 100 replaces frailty identification with condition discrimination.
Inferring missing cohort members from neighboring IDs or file order turns provenance into an untested assumption.
Selecting the grid phase or lifetime-spread scenario after seeing target outcomes invalidates prospective pair power.
Using an adaptive trigger derived from the same candidate score without a frozen rule couples feature development to endpoint ascertainment.
If dense RPTs change degradation beyond a predeclared equivalence margin, the schedule cannot validate the original process.
minimumValidation: Use a manifest-verified same-condition block, preserve at least 24 observed events, run the fixed 25-cycle endpoint register after the nominal cycle-480 feature landmark, document calibrated channel randomization, and require at least 100 non-tied within-block pairs before fitting. A lower-burden 50-cycle branch is eligible only with 36 usable events. Independently reproduce the pair count and final rank test.
simultaneousImpact: The design turns sample count, inspection timing, intervention burden, and provenance into joint gates for RUL prediction, bounded digital twins, accelerated-life frailty, and autonomous experiment selection. It prevents all four fields from mistaking abundant files or accurate fits for identifiable individual-state evidence.
surfaceSimilarityRisk: Not every repeated-measures problem has a pair ceiling or a measurement intervention. The connection applies only when inference is blocked within comparable groups and observation timing can tie outcomes or alter the system.
validationStatus: The combinatorial and provenance bottlenecks are verified on public artifacts. The proposed prospective battery schedule, measurement-equivalence claim, and lifetime-coordinate transport remain untested.
